messages:
maria: quick follow-up from the runtime facades RFC — i sketched a minimal operator contract for hosted/dedicated/private, want feedback on responsibilities and failure semantics
jonathan: thanks, dropping in. can you paste the sketch?
maria: sure — goal: single thin translation layer per env that maps our control-plane manifest -> runtime API. idea: minimal surface so each env can implement fast. example manifest snippet:
```yaml
deployment_mode: hosted # hosted|dedicated|private
model: gpt-4o-redwood:v1
qos:
  latency_slo_ms: 120
  throughput: 250rps
routing:
  fallback_model: gpt-4o-redwood:v1-small
security:
  kms: customer_key | redwood_managed
```
maria: the runtime facade would expose: Capabilities(), LoadModel(manifest), ServeRequest(req), EvictModel(model), MetricsStream() — that's it
sam: +1 on small surface. question: who owns autoscaling decisions for dedicated vs private? control plane or the runtime operator?
priya: for dedicated i'd favor operator-owned autoscaler with control-plane policy constraints (min/max) — private can be operator OR customer depending on deployment mode. hosted = our autoscaler
jonathan: sounds right. we should define invariants though: e.g., control plane must be able to force-evict a model in < 30s for security incidents. is that acceptable for private?
maria: good call. add forced-evict requirement to contract. for private we document best-effort and recommend heartbeat interval config in manifest
alex: telemetry + billing: how do we make usage signals compatible across environments? hosted has token counts, private might not send tokens off-network. need local aggregates and a reconciliation endpoint.
maria: propose telemetry contract: MetricsStream pushes aggregated counters every 10s; if env is private-without-egress, runtime persists deltas to disk and operator runs reconciliation job to push when allowed. control plane accepts signed reconciliation uploads
priya: also add capability discovery: runtime returns supported_quant, kv_cache_supported, max_seq_len. that avoids runtime probing at serve time
sam: on failure modes: if runtime can't honor latency_slo due to load we should have two policies: degrade_to_fallback_model OR queue-with-timeout. which should be default?
jonathan: prefer fallback for user-facing, but queue for batch jobs. the manifest needs a 'degrade_policy' field
maria: added degrade_policy in sketch. Also: model variant compatibility — runtime must advertise compatibility tags so control plane can pick compatible fallback without retranscoding
alex: one more: network isolation for private -> runtime should implement an access-check endpoint so control plane can validate identity without direct egress. e.g., local-signed nonce flow
maria: noted. that will be a lightweight /validate-identity endpoint that returns signed assertion limited to 5m
infra-bot: deployment-checker: validation rule suggestion: disallow hosted-managed kms when deployment_mode==private
priya: +1 infra-bot, also we need a migration path: v1 facade already used by hosted. plan: keep v1 facade stable, add optional capabilities endpoint in v2 and a translation shim in control plane for older runtimes
jonathan: how do we test compliance across vendors? propose smoke tests: start->load->inference->evict, plus QoS stress harness that can assert fallback or queue behaviors under load
sam: agree. add deterministic check: Capabilities().max_seq_len >= model.max_seq_len or fail at deploy time
maria: next steps I suggest: 1) formalize operator contract doc (this thread as initial notes) 2) implement Capabilities + MetricsStream in hosted runtime adapter 3) add reconciliation flow for private 4) create smoke tests and a weekly compliance run
jonathan: timeline?
maria: aiming for RFC v2 in 2 weeks, prototype in hosted runtime in 6 weeks
alex: callout: product needs clear docs on what customers can expect in private (e.g., forced-evict best-effort)
priya: i'll draft the customer-facing matrix
maria: cool — will convert these notes into a short doc. tagging @jonathan @sam for review when i post it
john: (small nit) please include exact error codes for EvictModel when it can't complete
maria: good point, will add an error code appendix
jonathan: thanks everyone.
